| [CLAIM-1167](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1167.md) v2 | Perspectives given as graded participation functions on a common measure overlap by the integral of their pointwise minimum, which is zero exactly when the measures they carve out are mutually singular and, for probability densities, equals one minus their total-variation distance, so separation of perspectives comes by degrees and need not be a partition | A26 and A29 of the exchange "Explain First Contact RL" (2026-11-22). A perspective is modelled as a participation function p_i: X → [0, 1] over a common measure μ, with submeasure μ_i = p_i μ, and the p_i need not sum to 1, which "would force a partition of the organization among perspectives" (A26). Two probability measures are mutually singular when a measurable set carries all of one and none of the other: "a perfect measurable distinction separates them". A29: overlap O_μ(p_i, p_j) = ∫ min(p_i, p_j) dμ is zero exactly when μ_i ⊥ μ_j. The assistant (Claude, in this session) supplied the proof and added that, for probability densities, the overlap is 1 − TV, so it is a standard affinity.
